title: What remainders do two numbers leave together?
description: One number leaves remainder three when divided by seven, and another leaves five. Writing them with letters shows the remainders of their sum, their take away and their multiplication.
teaching_notes: One idea: write each number as seven times something plus its remainder, then multiply out and pull seven out of what is left. Watch for students who add or multiply the remainders and stop, forgetting that the result can be larger than seven.

source: Figure it Out (identities and patterns, question 6)
video_script.why: The child can multiply out two brackets, but has not yet used letters to follow remainders through a sum, a take away and a multiplication.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as seven times a whole number plus its remainder, then multiply out the way the cards in the book did.
video_script.anchor: the two numbers of the book's question, one leaving remainder three and one leaving remainder five when divided by seven
video_script.payoff_line: The sum leaves remainder one, the take away leaves two, and the multiplication leaves one.

final_answer.value: Sum: remainder 1; difference: remainder 2 (or 5 the other way round); product: remainder 1
final_answer.spoken: the sum leaves remainder one, the take away leaves two, and the multiplication leaves one

maths_rules: take away: (7b + 5) − (7a + 3) = 7b − 7a + 2 = 7(b − a) + 2, remainder 2; the other way round (7a + 3) − (7b + 5) = 7(a − b) − 2 = 7(a − b − 1) + 5, remainder 5
video_script.design: One idea: write each number as seven times a whole number plus its remainder, and pull seven out of the working. The two numbers stay on the board. The last regrouping, for the multiplication, is left until the answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='first'/>One number leaves remainder three when divided by seven.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Another number leaves remainder five when divided by seven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What remainder do we get from their sum, their take away, and their multiplication?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a row of 7 counters repeated three times with 3 left over, labelled 7a + 3; a row of 7 counters repeated four times with 5 left over, labelled 7b + 5

narration: <bookmark mark='groups'/>Divide by seven. Some full groups of seven are made, and a few are left over.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first number is seven times eigh, plus three.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second is seven times b, plus five.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers seven eigh plus three, and seven b plus five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the remainder of their sum, take away and multiplication when divided by 7

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the remainders of their sum, take away and multiplication.

marks.out: 8 is split as 7 + 1, and 7(a + b + 1) + 1 is written
marks.rem: the 1 left after the bracket is marked as the remainder

beats.colours: the multiples of 7 in one colour, the remainder in another
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, the sum. Seven eigh plus three plus seven b plus five is seven eigh plus seven b plus eight.
<bookmark mark='out'/>Eight is seven plus one. Seven comes out of three parts, giving seven times eigh plus b plus one, plus one.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>The remainder is one.

beats.on_screen: Take away: (7b + 5) - (7a + 3) = 7b - 7a + 2 = 7(b - a) + 2. The other way round: (7a + 3) - (7b + 5) = 7(a - b) - 2 = 7(a - b - 1) + 5

marks.rem: 7(b - a) + 2 is written, with 2 marked as the remainder
marks.five: -2 is written as -7 + 5, giving 7(a - b - 1) + 5, with 5 marked as the remainder

beats.colours: the multiples of 7 in one colour, the remainder in another
narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step two, the take away. Seven b plus five, minus seven eigh plus three, is seven b minus seven eigh plus two.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>That is seven times b minus eigh, plus two. The remainder is two.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Taken the other way round, we get seven times eigh minus b, minus two.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Minus two is minus seven plus five. The remainder is five.

marks.all: 49ab + 35a + 21b + 15 is written as the whole expansion

beats.colours: the four parts in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, the multiplication. Every term meets every term. Seven eigh times seven b is forty nine eigh b. Seven eigh times five is thirty five eigh.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Three times seven b is twenty one b. Three times five is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='all'/>We get forty nine eigh b plus thirty five eigh plus twenty one b plus fifteen.

beats.on_screen: Check with 10 and 12: 10 = 7 + 3 and 12 = 7 + 5. Sum 22 = 21 + 1. Take away 12 - 10 = 2. Multiplication 10 x 12 = 120 = 119 + 1

marks.sum: 22 = 21 + 1 is written and ticked, and 12 - 10 = 2 is written and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='pick'/>Step four, put the answers back in the question, with two numbers. Ten leaves three, and twelve leaves five.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Their sum is twenty two, which is twenty one plus one. Twelve minus ten is two.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Ten times twelve is one hundred twenty, which is one hundred nineteen plus one.

beats.on_screen: Answer: sum, remainder 1; take away, remainder 2 (or 5 the other way round); multiplication: 49ab + 35a + 21b + 15 = 7(7ab + 5a + 3b + 2) + 1, remainder 1
narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Fifteen is fourteen plus one, so seven comes out of the rest.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum leaves remainder one, the take away leaves two, and the multiplication leaves one.
